title: Building a cigar-box guitar; Maxey's first guitar
summary: Pete began in 1934 on a homemade copper-wire guitar; Maxey recalls starting on a twelve-string.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Picking up a first guitar or banjo, self-taught

blocks.x: And when did you start in the music business? Did you just grab a musical?

Well, I started in the music business in 1934. 1934. 1934. 1934. And when did you start learning? Well, I just picked on up from then. Just start learning. I made my first guitar. Yeah, you made it yourself? I made it myself. That's what I learned on. Yeah. From that on, then I went and bought me old cheap box. Mm-hmm. I learned and I just went on out. What kind of guitar did you make? How many strings? Well, I made a five-string guitar. A five-string? I had a copper wire with a cigar bar.
What about that fifth string? Did it look like this? The same as the regular sixth string?
They were all six-string, but they weren't rapped. Mm-hmm. Just plain naked string, copper wire.
Oh, I see. Just like these strings, not like a five-string banjo. That's right, yeah. I see. And, Maxie, what was your first instrument?
Yeah. And then you took up guitar. What kind of guitar did you have? You told me.
Twelve-string. You started on twelve strings. Started on the twelve. Iris King, that's the name of the box.
